long_biography.plain_text:
In 2000, Fatkhullin's company began with FX Charts, a lower-cost application aimed at foreign-exchange brokers. It followed with the MQL programming language, allowing users to write trading robots, before adding futures and mobile terminals. He was already chief executive when MetaTrader 4 emerged from an eighteen-month development cycle in 2005.

MetaTrader 4's redesigned architecture and MQL4 tools made automated strategies central to the product ecosystem. MetaTrader 5 widened the model to stocks and futures, while MQL5.com added code libraries, markets and freelance services around the platform. More recently, Fatkhullin has moved the business further into institutional infrastructure with an ultra-low-latency matching engine for liquidity aggregation, execution and risk management.

uncertainties: No dedicated Forbes.com profile or credible Forbes identity match was found after exact Latin-name, Cyrillic-name, MetaQuotes, billionaire and profile searches.

Renat Fatkhullin is not unique. A Russian entertainer associated with KVN, construction professionals and name-only directory profiles were rejected because they lack the combined MetaQuotes, MQL5, Cyprus and Ultency anchors. The target's Cyrillic spelling is Ренат Фатхуллин; occasional Latin rendering as Renat Fathullin is treated as a transliteration variant only when the MetaQuotes anchor is present.

No reliable full patronymic, middle name, exact birthplace, birth country or date of birth was verified. Russian nationality does not prove birth in Russia, so no birth field is proposed; patronymics attached to construction namesakes were not imported.

The immutable record's LinkedIn URL resolves to the same Cyprus MetaQuotes profile and is therefore retained rather than re-proposed. No verified personal Instagram account or standalone personal website was found; the MetaQuotes site is proposed only as a Company Website.

The immutable vessel relationships to MetaQuotes and Ultency were used only as distinctive identity clues. Vessel ownership, names, values, locations and dimensions are excluded from the biographies and classifications.

Independent and official sources continue to identify Fatkhullin as MetaQuotes CEO through February 2026, and no credible founder-exit report was found. This supports continuing leadership, but it does not establish his exact current equity percentage or sole beneficial ownership of the private company.

The Cyprus register-derived page lists Fatkhullin as a director of MetaQuotes Ltd, not as a shareholder. Directorship is not converted into a personal ownership percentage, and the page itself cautions that public officer data may not be fully current.

MetaTrader, MQL, MQL5.com, Ultency, company offices, customer relationships and intellectual property are MetaQuotes corporate products or assets. They support Fatkhullin's founder biography but are not represented as his personal property or independently valued.

MetaQuotes led Sumsub's $6 million 2020 funding round and bought an early investor's shares. The transaction is attributed to MetaQuotes, not to Fatkhullin personally, and no current personal Sumsub holding is inferred.

A CySEC-hosted Hellenic Bank prospectus records Fatkhullin with a direct 5.98% stake in September 2012. That dated filing does not establish a current holding, so the bank stake is treated as historical context and excluded from current-industry and wealth-relationship classifications.

The Self-made classification rests on Fatkhullin's documented founding and long-term operation of MetaQuotes. No credible inheritance or family-enterprise evidence was found, but the sources do not establish his starting capital, family resources or enough formative detail for a narrower subtype.

Blank title, middle name, suffix, secondary residence, birth, death, age, internal-note and unknown-name fields remain unsupported, optional, inapplicable or system-managed rather than enrichment targets.
